title: Customs Tariff Amendment (Incorporation of Proposals and Other Measures) Bill 2024
short_title: Customs Tariff Amendment (Incorporation of Proposals and Other Measures) Bill 2024

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would amend the Customs Tariff Act 1995 to abolish over 450 nuisance tariffs, extend duty-free access for goods from Ukraine and remove spent phased-rate provisions.
It would set the general duty rate on those headings and subheadings to Free from 1 July 2024 and extend the Ukraine concession by 24 months to 3 July 2026.
Parts 1 and 2 would commence retrospectively on 1 July and 4 July 2024 to match earlier Customs Tariff Proposals, while Part 3 would commence 28 days after Royal Assent.
changes: Part 1 would set the customs duty rate to Free for over 450 tariff headings and subheadings in Schedule 3, applying to goods imported on or after 1 July 2024.
Part 1 would also revise Schedule 14 so that preferential rates for goods originating under the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP) Agreement are no higher than the general rate.
Part 2 would extend the temporary duty reduction for goods that are the produce or manufacture of Ukraine to 3 July 2026, keeping existing exceptions for goods such as alcohol, fuel and tobacco.
Part 3 would repeal spent phased-rate table items in Schedules 10 and 11 for Korean and Japanese originating goods, and redundant paragraphs of section 11.
Abolishing the tariffs is estimated to cut receipts by $41.0 million over four years from 2024-25, and the Ukraine extension by $2.0 million over two years.
summary.affected: Importers of goods such as toothbrushes, tools, fridges and clothing, importers of goods from Ukraine, and traders using the RCEP, Korea and Japan trade agreements are affected.
